mathcounts-potw-2025-12-22-01.prompt: Kathryn realized that she is in a time-crunch to get some of her holiday shopping completed. She needs to have all of it done by this time tomorrow. As she looks over her schedule for the next 24 hours, she sees that she will be spending $\frac13$ of it sleeping, $\frac13$ of it at school and $\frac18$ of it working at her part-time job. How much of the next 24 hours is left over for shopping? Express your answer as a common fraction.

mathcounts-potw-2025-12-22-02.prompt: Kathryn was given a \$25 gift certificate to the music store. She decides to use it to buy her brother a CD. The tax on her purchase will be 4.5%. If Kathryn wants to ensure that her gift certificate covers her entire purchase (including the tax), what is the most amount of dollars that can be in the price of her purchase before the tax is added? Express your answer to the nearest hundredth.

mathcounts-potw-2025-12-22-03.prompt: Kathryn saw her mother put 4 teaspoons of baking soda into a bowl. The cookie recipe only calls for $1\frac13$ teaspoons of baking soda, but her mother explained that she was making more than one batch at a time. If the recipe calls for $\frac12$ teaspoon of vanilla, how many teaspoons of vanilla does Kathryn now expect her mother to put into the bowl?
